issues.legal_issue: A court may mould relief after trial to provide an appropriate remedy and avoid further litigation, provided the moulded relief does not take an affected party by surprise or cause prejudice.

An appellate court reviewing a trial court’s exercise of discretion to mould relief should not re-examine every detail absent prejudice or grave injustice, and review in a further appeal should be minimal.

Relief setting aside the purchasers’ sale deeds and protecting the testamentary disposition could be moulded in the circumstances even though the suit was brought by the trust and the trust was not entitled to the declaratory relief sought.
A court auction sale and the resulting sale deed, remaining unchallenged and intact, transferred title to the purchaser and prevented a later devisee from conveying title to the property.
